'''Fabiola Gianotti''' ({{IPA|it|faˈbiːola dʒaˈnɔtti|lang}}; born 29 October 1960) is an Italian experimental [[particle physicist]] who served as [[Director general|Director-General]] of the [[CERN|European Organization for Nuclear Research]] (CERN) from 2016 to 2026.

== Early life and education ==
From an early age, Gianotti was interested in nature and the world around her. Her mother, from Sicily, encouraged Gianotti in the fine arts. Her father, an acclaimed [[geologist]] from Piedmont, encouraged her early love of learning and encouraged her scientific interests.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.humans-of-science.org/single-post/2018/01/30/Doctor-Fabiola-Gianotti-on-being-the-first-female-director-of-the-greatest-fundamental-science-experiment-on-earth|title=Humans of Science (HoS) {{!}} Single Post|website=Humans of Science (HoS)|language=en|access-date=17 July 2018|archive-date=17 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180717212730/https://www.humans-of-science.org/single-post/2018/01/30/Doctor-Fabiola-Gianotti-on-being-the-first-female-director-of-the-greatest-fundamental-science-experiment-on-earth|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=9 November 2014 |title=Fabiola Gianotti: woman with the key to the secrets of the universe {{!}} Observer profile |url=http://www.theguardian.com/theobserver/2014/nov/09/fabiola-gianotti-new-director-general-cern |access-date=29 March 2022 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref>

Gianotti found her passion for [[scientific research]] after reading a biography of [[Marie Curie]]. Previously, she had studied the [[humanities]], focusing on music and philosophy at the [[Liceo classico]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/theobserver/2014/nov/09/fabiola-gianotti-new-director-general-cern|title=Fabiola Gianotti: woman with the key to the secrets of the universe {{!}} Observer profile|last=McKie|first=Robin|date=9 November 2014|website=the Guardian|language=en|access-date=17 July 2018}}</ref> Gianotti received a [[PHD|PhD]] in experimental particle physics from the [[Physics]] department of the [[University of Milan]] in 1989.<ref name=PassionPiano>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/03/07/science/fabiola-gianotti-physics-cern.html |title=A Celebrated Physicist With a Passion for Music - The New York Times |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=7 March 2018 |access-date=20 April 2019|last1=Sciolino |first1=Elaine }}</ref>

== Life and career ==

=== Academic and professional career ===

Since 1996, Gianotti has worked at [[CERN]], starting with a fellowship and continuing to become a full-time research physicist. In 2009 she was promoted to project leader and Spokesperson of the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS Collaboration]]. She also worked on the [[WA70 experiment|WA70]], [[UA2 experiment|UA2]] and [[ALEPH experiment|ALEPH]] experiments at CERN, where she was involved in detector development, software development and data analysis. In 2016 she was elected to be the first female Director-General of CERN. She has since been reappointed for a second term, which ended in 2025.<ref name="reelection">{{cite web |date=6 November 2019 |title=CERN Council appoints Fabiola Gianotti for second term of office as CERN Director General |url=https://home.cern/news/press-release/cern/cern-council-appoints-fabiola-gianotti-second-term-office-cern-director |access-date=16 March 2020 |website=CERN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://home.cern/about/who-we-are/our-people/biographies/fabiola-gianotti-born-1960-italian|title=Fabiola Gianotti (born in 1960) {{!}} CERN|website=home.cern|access-date=9 February 2020}}</ref>

She has been a member of several international committees, such as the Scientific Council of the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dgdr.cnrs.fr/bo/2006/02-06/comi-bo0206-adu29-11-2005.htm|title=Arrêté du 29 novembre 2005 portant nomination au conseil scientifique du Centre national de la recherche scientifique|website=CNRS|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150831134926/http://www.dgdr.cnrs.fr/bo/2006/02-06/comi-bo0206-adu29-11-2005.htm|archive-date=31 August 2015|access-date=31 August 2015}}</ref> in France, the Physics Advisory Committee of [[Fermilab]] in the US, the Council of the [[European Physical Society]], the Scientific Council of the [[DESY]] Laboratory<ref name=":4">{{cite web|url=http://www.sab-2014-berlin.de/scientific-advisory-board/mitglieder/|title=The members of the Scientific Advisory Board|publisher=German Commission for UNESCO|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140321020622/http://www.sab-2014-berlin.de/scientific-advisory-board/mitglieder/|archive-date=21 March 2014|access-date=31 August 2015}}</ref> in Germany, and the Scientific Advisory Committee of [[NIKHEF]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nikhef.nl/en/about-nikhef/background-information/organisation-structure/scientific-advisory-committee-sac/|title=Scientific Advisory Committee (SAC)|website=NIKHEF|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150831142307/https://www.nikhef.nl/en/about-nikhef/background-information/organisation-structure/scientific-advisory-committee-sac/|archive-date=31 August 2015|access-date=31 August 2015}}</ref> in the Netherlands. She is a member of the Scientific Advisory Board<ref name=":4" /> of the UN Secretary-General. She was elected a Foreign Member of the [[Royal Society]] (ForMemRS) in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2018/05/distinguished-scientists-elected-fellows-royal-society-2018/|title=Distinguished scientists elected as Fellows and Foreign Members of the Royal Society |publisher=The Royal Society|date=9 May 2018|access-date=10 May 2018 }}</ref>

Gianotti is also a member of the Italian Academy of Sciences ([[Accademia dei Lincei|Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]]),{{citation needed|date=March 2020}} a foreign associate member of the [[National Academy of Sciences|US National Academy of Sciences]] and foreign associate of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]. She was also elected a Member of the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 2019. Since 2013, she is an honorary professor at the [[University of Edinburgh]].<ref name="ProfEd">{{cite web|url=http://www.ed.ac.uk/news/staff/appointments-awards/2013/fabiola-gianotti-260813|title=Honorary Professor: Fabiola Gianotti|website=University of Edinburgh|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150828143732/http://www.ed.ac.uk/news/staff/appointments-awards/2013/fabiola-gianotti-260813|archive-date=28 August 2015|access-date=28 August 2015}}</ref> She is associated with the Experimental Particle Physics Group in the [[School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Edinburgh|School of Physics and Astronomy]]<ref name="ProfEd"/> and also a member of the International Advisory Committee of the [[peter Higgs|Higgs]] Centre for [[Theoretical physics|Theoretical Physics]] at the University of Edinburgh.<ref name="ProfEd"/>

Gianotti also appeared in the 2013 documentary film ''[[Particle Fever]]'' about work at the [[Large Hadron Collider]] at CERN.

Gianotti is a member of the Board of Trustees of the [[World Economic Forum]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leadership and Governance - World Economic Forum |url=https://www.weforum.org/about/leadership-and-governance/}}</ref>

Gianotti was appointed{{When|date=January 2026}} Director-General of CERN for a five-year term beginning on 1 January 2016, making her the first woman to hold the position.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fabiola Gianotti signs her contract as CERN's new Director-General |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/1976432 |access-date=28 August 2015 |website=CERN Bulletin}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Castelvecchi |first1=Davide |year=2014 |title=Higgs hunter will be CERN's first female director: Italian physicist Fabiola Gianotti will take the reins at the European physics powerhouse in 2016. |journal=Nature |doi=10.1038/nature.2014.16287 |s2cid=124442791 |doi-access=free}}</ref> At its 195th Session in 2019, the CERN Council selected Gianotti for a second term as Director-General. This is the first time in CERN's history that a Director-General has been appointed for a full second term.<ref name="reelection" />

=== Higgs boson discovery ===
During Gianotti's time as project leader and spokesperson of ATLAS, the experiment was one of two involved in the observation of the [[Higgs boson]]. On 4 July 2012 Gianotti announced the discovery of the particle. Until the observation, the Higgs boson was a purely theoretical part of the [[Standard Model]] of particle physics. Gianotti's deep understanding of the ATLAS experiment, and her leadership, were recognised as major factors in the discovery.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|url = http://www.iop.org/about/awards/hon_fellowship/hon_fellows/page_68416.html|title = Dr Fabiola Gianotti, CERN|access-date = 3 May 2017|website = IOP Institute of Physics}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/1734377?ln=en|title = ATLAS makes a smooth changeover at the top|access-date = 28 August 2015|website = CERN Courier}}</ref>

=== Publications ===
Gianotti is the author or co-author of more than 500 publications in [[peer review]]ed scientific journals.<ref name=hep>{{INSPIRE-HEP author}}</ref> She has given more than 30 invited plenary talks at the major international conferences in the field.{{citation needed|date=February 2019}}

Some of her most notable publications include "Observation of a New Particle in the Search for the Standard Model Higgs Boson with the ATLAS Detector at the LHC", where CERN presented the Higgs boson observation,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=The ATLAS Collaboration|date=31 August 2012|title=Observation of a New Particle in the Search for the Standard Model Higgs Boson with the ATLAS Detector at the LHC|journal=European Organisation for Nuclear Research (Cern)|volume=716|issue=1|pages=1–29|arxiv=1207.7214|doi=10.1016/j.physletb.2012.08.020|bibcode=2012PhLB..716....1A| s2cid=119169617 }}</ref> "Searches for supersymmetry at high-energy colliders: the past, the present and the future" in the IOP Science, [[New Journal of Physics]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Gianotti|first=Fabiola|date=August 2002|title=Searches for supersymmetry at high-energy colliders: the past, the present and the future|journal=New Journal of Physics|language=en|volume=4|issue=1|pages=63|doi=10.1088/1367-2630/4/1/363|bibcode=2002NJPh....4...63G|issn=1367-2630|doi-access=free}}</ref> and "Calorimetry for particle physics" in the [[American Physical Society|APS]] Physics Journal.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fabjan|first1=Christian W.|last2=Gianotti|first2=Fabiola|date=15 October 2003|title=Calorimetry for particle physics|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=75|issue=4|pages=1243–1286|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.75.1243|bibcode=2003RvMP...75.1243F|url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/692252}}</ref>

=== Work environment ===
{{See also|Women in science}}
Gianotti had to push past barriers to be successful in a male-dominated field. In the European scientific community, for every one woman, there are two men. Only 20% of the team that worked on the [[ATLAS experiment|ATLAS]] project were women.<ref name=":0" /> Gianotti was the first female Director-General of CERN, and she led two of the largest [[CERN]] experiments in 2012. She insists that she has never faced discrimination because of her gender, saying "I cannot say myself that I ever felt discriminated against ... Perhaps I was but I didn't realize it." Gianotti is helping break down barriers the male-dominated field created for aspiring [[Women in science|female scientists]].<ref name=PassionPiano/> She specifically wants to give women more support when having children. She feels that she was never given enough support, and for this reason, never had children, a decision she now regrets.<ref name=":0" />

Gianotti was included among the 'Top 100 most inspirational women' by ''[[The Guardian]]'' newspaper in 2011,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2011/mar/08/fabiola-gianotti-100-women |title=Top 100 women: science and medicine |access-date=28 August 2015 |website=Guardian News |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150416061313/http://www.theguardian.com/science/2011/mar/08/fabiola-gianotti-100-women |archive-date=16 April 2015 }}</ref> ranked fifth in [[Time (magazine)|''Time'' magazine's]] 'Personality of the Year' in 2012, was the runner-up for ''Time'' magazine's 'Person of the Year' in the same year,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://poy.time.com/2012/12/19/runner-up-fabiola-gianotti-the-discoverer/ |title=Runner-Up: Fabiola Gianotti, the Discoverer |access-date=28 August 2015 |magazine=Time |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150321211606/http://poy.time.com/2012/12/19/runner-up-fabiola-gianotti-the-discoverer/ |archive-date=21 March 2015 }}</ref> was included among the 'Top 100 most influential women' by ''[[Forbes]]'' magazine in 2013,<ref name=":2">{{cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/fabiola-gianotti/ |title=#83 Fabiola Gianotti |access-date=28 August 2015 |website=Forbes |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150531154622/http://www.forbes.com/profile/fabiola-gianotti/ |archive-date=31 May 2015 }}</ref> and was considered among the 'Leading Global Thinkers of 2013' by [[Foreign Policy|''Foreign Policy'' magazine]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://2013-global-thinkers.foreignpolicy.com/gianotti |title=François Englert, Peter Higgs, and Fabiola Gianotti |access-date=28 August 2015 |website=The FP Group |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150828134143/http://2013-global-thinkers.foreignpolicy.com/gianotti |archive-date=28 August 2015 }}</ref>

=== Comic Sans controversy ===
When CERN announced the discovery of the [[Higgs boson]], some controversy sprang from Gianotti's use of the [[Comic Sans]] typeface in the presentation of the results.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.designweek.co.uk/issues/may-2012/the-power-of-type-or-why-not-to-use-comic-sans-to-present-a-scientific-breakthrough/|title=The power of type (or why not to use Comic Sans to present a scientific breakthrough)|first=Emily|last=Gosling|date=5 July 2012}}</ref> Alby Reid, a physicist, started an online petition calling for Microsoft to change the name of the font to Comic Cerns.<ref name="huffingtonpost.co.uk">{{cite web|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/2012/07/06/change-name-of-comic-sans_n_1653774.html |title=Change Name Of Comic Sans To 'Comic Cerns' Say Physicists After Higgs Boson Discovery &#124; HuffPost UK |publisher=Huffingtonpost.co.uk |date= 6 July 2012|access-date=20 April 2019}}</ref> [[Vincent Connare]], the font's creator, tweeted support for the petition.<ref name="huffingtonpost.co.uk"/> Gianotti had used Comic Sans in previous presentations, but the controversy was generated due to the importance of the material presented.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.newscientist.com/blogs/shortsharpscience/2012/07/comic-sans-at-cern.html |title=Higgs in Comic Sans: the right font for physics? |access-date=31 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171118102947/https://www.newscientist.com/blogs/shortsharpscience/2012/07/comic-sans-at-cern.html |archive-date=18 November 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Gianotti is a trained ballerina and plays the [[Piano]]. She has never been married; in a profile on Gianotti in ''[[The New York Times]]'', the Dutch engineer Rende Steerenberg described her as someone who "has dedicated her life to physics... sure, she has made sacrifices."<ref name=PassionPiano/>

In a 2010 interview, Gianotti said that she saw no contradiction between science and faith, and that they belong to "two different spheres".<ref>{{cite web|title=La signora dell'universo|url=http://www.famigliacristiana.it/articolo/scienziata.aspx|publisher=[[Famiglia Cristiana]]|language=it|date=20 August 2010}}</ref> In an interview by ''[[la Repubblica]]'', she said that "science and religion are separate disciplines, though not antithetical. You can be a physicist and have faith or not. It is better for [[God]] and science to keep the right distance."<ref>{{cite web|title="Io, tra Dio e il Big Bang". Fabiola Gianotti, direttrice del Cern: la signora dell'Universo|url=http://www.repubblica.it/scienze/2014/12/28/news/io_tra_dio_e_il_big_bang_fabiola_giannotti_direttrice_del_cern_la_signora_dell_universo_di_dario_cresto-dina-103841329/|publisher=la Repubblica|language=it|date=28 December 2014}}</ref>

As of September 2020, she is a member of the Italian [[Aspen Institute]].<ref>[https://www.aspeninstitute.it/istituto/comunita-aspen/comitato-esecutivo executive Committee] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009043826/https://www.aspeninstitute.it/istituto/comunita-aspen/comitato-esecutivo |date=9 October 2010 }}, aspeninstitute.it/</ref>
